about: What the best of the field does for each thing the kit does, how the kit compares, and the tests that prove it. docs/benchmarks.md says how this is used; scripts/benchmarks.js holds it to that.

entries.what: Changing one setting precisely

leaders.does: Shift for finer resolution while dragging, type a value with the digits, Delete or double-click for the default, Enter and Esc to confirm or cancel
Double-click text entry of parameter values

entries.ours: Drag the number or its line; Shift for a tenth the speed, or always fine by preference; wheel and arrows by a step; double-click the number or press Enter to type, with units and k understood; a digit starts a value with no click; Delete or a double-click on the line for the default; the range and the default are shown while it is held. A range that rounds to many steps, such as a frequency in whole hertz, drags and scrolls across its whole range like any other; only a setting of a few steps moves a step at a time. A number too wide for its column is drawn smaller.
proof: a slide along a value is one gesture for the host

entries.what: What a right-click on a setting offers

leaders.does: Copy and paste of bands and presets, also between instances

entries.ours: Type a value, return to the default (named), copy, paste, lock against presets. No automation or mapping commands: those are the host's here.
proof: a value's menu resets, copies, pastes and locks

entries.what: Binding a hardware control to a setting from inside the plugin

leaders.does: MIDI Learn associates any MIDI controller with any parameter

entries.ours: "Learn a controller" in a setting's menu: the setting waits, shown beside its name; move a knob and it is bound, shown as its number; "Forget" frees it; Escape stops the waiting. The controller moves the setting on the audio thread and the host hears it as a gesture. What was learned is saved with the project. One controller to a setting and a setting to a controller; channel is ignored; plain 7-bit controllers only, no pitch bend, aftertouch or 14-bit. In VST3 a controller arrives as a hidden parameter standing in for it, so it needs a host that asks for the mapping and sends the plugin MIDI. Tested in both formats' test hosts; not yet tried with hardware in a real host.

entries.what: Finding, trying, keeping and sharing sounds

leaders.does: A preset system in every plugin, with copy and paste of presets between instances
Presets kept as files in a folder of the person's own, which can be copied to another machine

entries.ours: A browser over the sheet: search, the plugin's own and one's own, a four-bar picture of each, hear one by pointing at it, press to keep it, save and delete one's own, lock a setting against them. One's own are files, one JSON file a preset, in a folder under the application data, so they can be copied and shared; where a host keeps none the page keeps them, and hands them over when it can. A preset naming settings this version lacks asks first. The path through the real webview is compiled in CI but has no test of its own there.

entries.what: Learning what a control does without a manual

leaders.does: Interactive help hints, and an extensive help file

entries.ours: The foot of the sheet names and explains whatever is under the pointer or has the keyboard, in a box that never changes size: a longer text is drawn smaller. Pointing at anything moves nothing. Every tooltip is the house's own, never the browser's: a tool says its name after a moment. Help only adds: with it on, tips come sooner and say more, and a setting gets a card with its range and where it rests.

entries.what: Being the right size on any screen

leaders.does: A resize button for interface size and scaling, and a full screen mode

entries.ours: The page is scaled by as much as the tighter direction of the window allows, then laid out as wide and as tall as the window is, so a window of another shape is filled: the glass and its picture take the room, and no empty band is left. Three densities trade the size of the numbers for room on the glass. No full screen.

entries.what: Knowing how loud it is, and whether it clipped

leaders.does: A large output level meter with a peak level readout

entries.ours: The number is the peak. Six segments break at -24, -12, -6, -3 and 0 dB with the top of the scale stretched; colour by zone; a clip lamp that stays lit until clicked; the hold is the person's to choose. The bar rises at once and falls at a steady pace the person chooses, and the number is the held peak, so a level that jumps every reading can still be read. The lamp remembers a clip; the number's colour says only where the level is now.

entries.what: Seeing what the plugin is doing to the sound

leaders.does: An interactive display that fills the window: bands are made and adjusted on it with the mouse, over a live spectrum

entries.ours: A glass a plugin draws on, redrawn as settings and meters move, purple where the held setting shapes it. It can be the control itself: dragged across and up for two settings, as one gesture. While audio runs it has the sound itself, the last thousand samples that came in and went out, about thirty times a second, with a spectrum of them and a way to hold a wave still; and the last four seconds of every meter. In VST3 the processor hands the sound to the controller when the host connects them, which needs both in one process, as hosts load them. That handover and the webview path are compiled and tested in parts; no test yet watches a waveform arrive in a real host.

entries.what: Hearing the sound without the plugin, from the plugin

leaders.does: A global bypass in the bottom bar that avoids clicks

entries.ours: kit::bypass(id) gives a plugin its own bypass. Both formats tell the host it is the bypass, so the host's button and the plugin's are one; the runner fades to the sound coming in over 10 ms and back, with the plugin still running so its tails are right on return. The header shows it as an On button and the glass dims. The dry sound is not delayed, so a plugin with latency will not line up during the fade.

entries.what: Blending the effect with the sound that came in

leaders.does: A Mix knob on the front panel for parallel processing without a second track
A mix for each band and for the whole plugin

entries.ours: kit::mix(id) is the one Mix: the same key, name, range and place in every plugin. Every plugin must ship it or say in its benchmark.json why it makes no sense there, and the check fails otherwise. The plugin does the blending, since only it knows what its dry signal is.
proof: a plugin ships a mix and a level match, or says why not

entries.what: Judging a change by its tone, not by its being louder

leaders.does: Auto Gain, which compensates the output for the level change the processing makes
Gain Match, which holds the processed level to the unprocessed for comparison

entries.ours: kit::level_match(id) with kit_dsp::Match: a button in the header, beside the bypass, that holds the level going out to the level coming in. It compares the two over 400 ms, eases over 150 ms so it cannot act as a compressor, holds through silence, reaches at most 24 dB, and sits before the output trim, which stays the person's own. It keeps listening while off, so it is right the moment it is switched on. Every plugin ships it or says why not. It matches level, not loudness as the ear weighs it.

entries.what: Hearing the middle or the sides alone, and weighing one against the other

leaders.does: Solo of the mid or the side signal, with Auto-Solo that solos the section whose control is being moved
Solo buttons for left, right, mid and side, and a stereo width control

entries.ours: kit::listen(id) and kit::balance(id) with kit_dsp::MidSide: Both, Mid and Side as pills on the glass beside the meters, and one Balance that turns the other half down and never either up, so with the output trim it sets the level of each. A solo comes in over 20 ms, without a step. Every plugin that works on mid and side ships both or says why not. There is no solo that follows the control being moved, as bx_digital has: the pills stay as set.

entries.what: Refining a modelled valve or transformer itself

leaders.does: A Bias control that emulates the bias of a valve amplifier, and a switch between triode and pentode
Six modelled line transformers to choose from, Strength for how nonlinear the transformer is, Crush for drive into it, Morph for even harmonics, and a wet/dry Mix

entries.ours: A window each, the same in every plugin that models one, opened from the foot of the sheet: Tube has Bias, Grid, Sag and Glow (kit_dsp::Tube), Transformer has Weight, Core, Grip and Roll (kit_dsp::Transformer). Each draws the curve its sound is made with, from the same numbers on both sides, and the curve moves as a setting does. At rest a valve is the plain curve and a transformer passes the sound exactly, so a plugin that gains a window sounds as it did. The way in shows a dot when anything inside is off its rest, and At rest puts the window back as one step to undo. The settings are ordinary ones: automated, learned, saved and in presets. Under True Iron in one respect: one transformer shaped by four settings, not six measured ones to choose from.
